body: are both version 1 and version 2 in use??

Yes. Version 1 is actively in use and is the one in example projects and adapted by 57 teams (now 60). Version 2 was just released as technically the simpler variation of Version 1. I recently created a Zenodo and NPM Package for version 2 which has received about 120 downloads during the past day. I expect about 200 to 400 repos to have it within the next upcoming few month.

**Edit:** I also forgot to mention that outside the people currently using it (which are vastly growing), I believe Stark Drones has hundreds of pieces of cloud software they might release under this same license which would further broaden it's usage.

> OSI Status: Not Submitted

Wait, didn't you submit it and then withdraw it?
That looks like an OSI submission to me: https://lists.opensource.org/pipermail/license-review_lists.opensource.org/2020-December/005042.html

Hi, like I said earlier in #1134 I submitted and withdraw it, but decided not to go w/ the voting process w/ them. I didn't know how to best word that because that wasn't an option on the form.

Also original date of submission for the OPNL license was on November 10th. Even for the secondary license the submission and withdrawal was also few days ago. This means the SPDX submissions were earlier. The team at SPDX were already aware of my recent submission to OSI. **I also want to point out that the link you inserted isn't well indexed by Google and includes personal emails regarding everybody involved.** I rather not link to that for that explicit privacy purpose.

Also, you have previously raised similar issues like https://github.com/EthicalSource/hippocratic-copyleft/issues/1 where you downvoted every response to you. You also downvoted my other pull request and you have made a response in regards to my license on choosealicense even though the pull request there was related to Ethical Source and didn't include any of my licenses. This further prevents well meaning discussion or civil discourse.

Best regards, Andrew

1) Actually the information you added is mostly irrelevant. If you can seen the previous comments by the SPDX team in my other pull requests, they seen the OSI thread and/or are already aware it has been submitted to OSI.
2) You made a mistake not checking the full thread and therefore posted information that was generally already known. You also made a similar mistake when you didn't do enough due diligence on the choosealicense pull request. Your tone is suggesting complete and utter rejection of what I have to say, that you already went on a defensive mode for issues irrelevant to it.
3) Outside of knowing that you as a general GitHub user, without legal experience, outside of the SPDX team rejects to this pull request, no new nor productive information was provided.

That said, I want to reiterate the point that the SPDX identifier is needed for:
- Reserving the OPNL and OPNL-2.0 symbols to prevent confusion in the future in config files
- Easier to add in the NPM CLI and other terminal command line interfaces that use the SPDX standard
- Many people are already using it, and **Stark Drones** might decide to release hundreds of pieces of its cloud software under it.
- It is growing, fulfills a general purpose, and with the inclusion of things like BUSL-1.1, I feel like this is closer to within the definition of open source.

Anyways, I already iterated my core points. Any counterclaims in regards to my core points and responses to them have mostly already been tackled. I feel as if plenty of due diligence on my side have been done in regards to the making of this license and my views related to it.

Yes, I also want to emphasize that my main point was that the original SPDX submissions were prior to OSI and that the team is already aware of the submission. Also I withdrew the OSI submission, and haven't asked to move to the OSI board approval process which is outside of community discussion. That said I would like potential OSI inclusion in the future, but this has less to do with the SPDX submissions. There are different boards within open source with different philosophies and voting procedures. This doesn't invalid the license or its need.

This has been discussed by the SPDX-legal team, the following is a summary as per the license inclusion guidelines:

Definitive factors: The license appears to meet most of these, with the note that it is not OSI-approved and assuming that v2 text isn't planned to be modified (and that the version number would be bumped if it was).

Other factors: 
1)  v2 does substantially comply with the definitions listed here (in light of the fact that we would consider the preamble not part of the license conditions and marked as “optional”). 
2) It is structured to be generally usable by anyone.
3) Based on a search for the license in Github, it does not appear to any actual use at this point in time. While you have pointed to plans to promote the license, that is not actual use.
5) it was submitted by the license steward

For the "other factors", we look at them with a "totality of the factors" lens. Given that, based in particular on it not meeting factor 3, we don’t think it should be added to the License List at present. That it could be reconsidered in the future if the license shows significant usage in the wild.

As a separate note - blocking someone from this issue because you don't like or don't agree with their comments is not appropriate. If any kind of moderation is needed, that should be handled by the SPDX leaders or at least be raised amongst the community. Unilateral decisions, particularly by someone who is not regularly involved in a community, is not the open source way.
I also want to reiterate if accepted, the OPNL2 config can be added to many software packages that Stark Drones personally runs which would then meet the 3 requirement.

re: blocking - you have missed my point, "If any kind of moderation is needed, that should be handled by the SPDX leaders or at least be raised amongst the community."
You made a unilateral decision, that is the part that is not appropriate.
Hi @jlovejoy I do apologise in that instance. Please note he also replied in places outside of my pull request on here instead. Regardless, perhaps I should have tried raising that issue first.

re: usage - this is the chicken/egg issue we have seen before and we understand and appreciate the desire to be able to use SPDX identifiers. However, we also need to make a call and we cannot simply accept every submission that comes through because someone says they think it will be used a lot (everyone thinks that ;)

You can always use LicenseRef as per the SPDX spec in the meantime. And re-submit once there is more actual use.

Hi @jlovejoy, my worry is I have like 225 cloud repositories for tools used by alot of developers that I may want to put the identifier in if Stark Drones decided to go that route. Plus with the people already using it, although it is not alot, questions arise in regards to what happens if somebody in the future tries submitting a license w/ the OPNL or OPNL-2 tag?

That is the whole chicken in the egg problem I'm having.

I think it's somewhat unlikely that someone would submit a license with the same identifier - while it feels like we get a lot of submissions (b/c we are woefully behind), it's not that many and not all are accepted. 
You could also use something like LicenseRef-OPNL-2.0 in the meantime, which would be a nice set up for if/when later it is re-submitted
